subject: storytime
title: The Gingerbread Man
about: The folk tale of the cookie who runs away from everyone until a sly fox offers him a ride across the river, told lightly: the fox eats the cookie in one bite and says yum. The repeating chant Run, run, as fast as you can makes it one of the easiest stories to read with expression. It is a public-domain story retold here in first-grade words, four pages long.
tip: Ask: why did the Gingerbread Man trust the fox when he ran away from everyone else?

book.author: a folk tale (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: A runaway cookie meets a sly fox.

passage.text:
A little old woman made a cookie.
It was a gingerbread man.
She put him in the oven to bake.
When she opened the oven, he jumped out!
He ran out the door.
"Run, run, as fast as you can!"
"You can't catch me, I'm the Gingerbread Man!"
The old woman ran after him.
But she could not catch him.
***
He ran past a cow.
"Stop!" said the cow.
"I want a bite!"
"Run, run, as fast as you can!"
"You can't catch me, I'm the Gingerbread Man!"
The cow ran after him.
But she could not catch him.
***
He ran past a horse.
"Stop!" said the horse.
"I want a bite!"
"Run, run, as fast as you can!"
"You can't catch me, I'm the Gingerbread Man!"
The horse ran after him.
But he could not catch him.
Then he came to a river.
He could not swim.
***
A fox came by.
"Hop on my tail," said the fox.
"I will take you across."
He hopped on.
"The water is deep," said the fox.
"Hop up on my back."
"Now hop up on my nose."
He hopped up on the fox's nose.
Snap!
The fox gobbled him up in one bite.
"Yum!" said the fox.
And that was the end of the Gingerbread Man.

cards.note: Gingerbread is a cookie made with ginger, a spice; smell some if you have it.

cards.q: What did the Gingerbread Man do when the oven opened?
cards.note: Out of the oven, out the door, and the chase begins.
The cow, the horse and the fox all want the same thing.

cards.q: What did the fox tell the Gingerbread Man to do?
cards.note: Tail, then back, then nose: each hop brings the cookie closer to the fox's mouth.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: Baked, ran, cow, horse, river, fox: ask him to say the order on his fingers.

cards.q: What happened at the end of the story?
cards.note: Snap, one bite, yum; that is how the story has always ended.

cards.q: What was the fox like in the story?
cards.note: The fox did not chase; he was sly and got the cookie to come to him.

cards.q: Where did the Gingerbread Man meet the fox?
cards.note: The river is the problem: a cookie cannot swim, and that is why he needed the fox.

cards.q: In the story, what does 'gobbled' mean?
cards.note: To gobble is to eat something fast and all at once, like a hungry turkey.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: He reads the three words himself; only one of them is in the story.
